title.narrative: Emergency WASH Response: Lifesaving Water, Sanitation Hygiene for Flood‑ and Drought‑Hit Communities in Beledweyne

description.narrative: ltpgtBeledweyne,a city bisected by the Shabelle River in central Somalia’s Hiraan region, is highly susceptible to both flooding and drought, which frequently undermine its urban water infrastructure. During the intense Gu rains from mid-April to mid-May 2024, severe flooding affected around 268,000 people and displaced approximately 81,000. This hydrological volatility severely disrupts the primary water supply for over 80,000 internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host families, who rely on shallow, privately managed or committee-run riverbank wells. These wells are often contaminated, silted, structurally damaged and unreliable, exacerbated by poor maintenance and flood impacts.ltbrgtIn response, this WASH project will serve 18,546, individuals—of whom 13,050 are IDPs and 5,496 are members of host communities, with women making up 54 percent of the total and around 742 people with disabilities across nine IDP sites and two neighboring villages. The initiative aims to restore reliable access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene services, reduce public health risks, and bolster local systems. Core interventions include rehabilitating and expanding water supply systems by repairing strategic shallow wells identified during a February 2025 infrastructure assessment and extending pipelines to underserved, densely populated settlements to minimize dependence on water trucking. The project also supplies WASH upgrades for two health facilities, one school, and a GBV one- stop center, alongside constructing 40 new gender-sensitive, flood-resilient, disability-accessible latrines and upgrading another 40 damaged units.ltbrgtFurther measures address solid waste management by establishing designated disposal pits, conducting systematic water-quality monitoring using portable test kits and laboratory collaboration, disinfecting water sources, and delivering participatory community hygiene promotion. The February assessment highlighted critical gaps: many key wells were broken or heavily degraded, distribution pipelines were insufficient in outlying settlements, and waste was being disposed of improperly, increasing contamination and disease risk. Coordination with local authorities, the ABC platform, the Beledweyne Water Supply Association, and the WASH Cluster will foster inclusion, sustainability, and accountability.ltbrgtBuilt on community consultations with IDPs, host communities, well owners, service providers, and informed by technical assessments, this intervention complements existing AICs-funded efforts. It focuses on restoring equitable access to safe, sufficient, and affordable water through shallow-well rehabilitation, pipeline expansions, and formal agreements with water service providers. These efforts are designed to reduce waterborne disease, enhance household resilience, align with the 2025 Somalia Humanitarian Response Plan, and ultimately improve public health and climate resilience in Beledweyne.ltbrgtlt/pgt
